In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we know very little about the IGM, but we know that there is a lot of it.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to measure the abundances of O VI and C IV in the high-redshift IGM with reasonable accuracy.
we have detected the first metals in the IGM at z ~3, and that we are starting to see a trend for higher metallicity at lower redshift.
we have measured abundances of oxygen, carbon, silicon, iron, and magnesium in the IGM at z ~2.5–5.5, but we still have a lot of work to do.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IGM is enriched by at least two different mechanisms, and that the relative contribution of these mechanisms varies with redshift.
